context: The bucket array is the same as in Figure 6-2. The text gives its capacity as 100 and the hash function as key % 100. Neither this figure nor the accompanying text gives the actual name for student ID 20336.
description: Under “Input key” on the left, 20336 appears in orange above 12836 in blue. Both curved paths pass through “Hash function: key % 100” and point to the bold index 36. A pink “Hash collision” label appears above their meeting point.

Under “Output value” on the right, the upper orange box and lower blue box both read “Xiao Ha.” The two tables below list the array contents and lookup results, respectively. Ellipses stand for the other buckets.

frames.explanation: The IDs end in the same two digits. The bucket index obtained by taking the remainder cannot tell us whether the full ID in the bucket matches. We must check the full key and use a collision resolution method.
frames.title: 20336 and 12836 collide in bucket 36

result: Chaining and open addressing can distinguish and store colliding keys. Expanding the table lowers the load and helps reduce collisions.
summary: Different student IDs can map to one bucket. Without collision handling, reading a value by bucket index alone can return the wrong result.
